newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finnish forestry stocks up on pulp hike hopes.
newsitem.headline: Finnish forestry stocks up on pulp hike hopes.

text.p: Shares in Finnish forest industry companies rose sharply on Monday as pulp producers said they may hike pulp prices, a key cyclical indicactor for the paper industry, brokers said.
Sentiment was also helped by an overall rally sparked by a Wall Street rebound overnight, they said.

At 1300/1000 GMT, the forest industry sub-index was 3.31 percent higher, although volume was thin with UPM-Kymmene the only lively share, trading up 3.50 markka or 3.33 percent at 108.00 markka in 12 million markka volume.
Enso advanced 3.81 percent or 1.60 markka to 43.60 and Metsa-Serla rose 3.38 percent or 1.20 markka to 36.70. Stromsdal rose 1.50 markka or over seven percent to 22.50 markka.

Pulp prices have been expected to rise this spring but Monday's news that some Swedish and Finnish producers were considering a hike was nonetheless good news, particularly in the light of the Finnish firms' previously cautious estimates, analysts said.
"This was a positive signal," one analyst said.
